precepts.text: In all the lands we were scattered, if we seek the Lord our God, he shall be found, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul, meaning do everything God says to do; when thou art in tribulation, even in the latter days. So these Christians don't know what they talking about. For the Lord thy God is a merciful God.
precepts.point: Sometime you think it's only the men they going after. Oh no, they getting the black woman too. So all you independent women, you just get ready. I love everybody, I don't see color; well, guess what? Color sees you.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.”

In all the lands we were scattered, “if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul”, meaning do everything God says to do. “When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice; (For the Lord thy God is a merciful God;) he will not forsake thee”.

When thou art in tribulation, even in the latter days: so these Christians don't know what they are talking about when they say the church won't be here. Israel is in tribulation in the latter days, and Jeremiah said “in the latter days ye shall consider it perfectly.” Our people will not repent unless they get a foot up their behind; death makes people reconsider their ways. We say we are Christians, we serve the same God, and the white man doesn't give a damn about that. But the Lord is merciful: seek him with all the heart and he will not forsake us nor forget the covenant of our fathers.

precepts.text: Keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people; our reputation for wisdom came from keeping the law.
precepts.point: It is no coincidence that Babylon used Daniel to advance itself and modern Babylon used a black man to lay out its capital; the slave masters knew that though captive we were not stupid, and Egypt, Persia, Greece, Rome and America all used the genius of the conquered.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
Where does that wisdom come from? “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” The commandments were our wisdom and understanding to do.

Read on: “For what nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them, as the Lord our God is in all things that we call upon him for? And what nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?” When we applied our commandments and our laws, the nations looked at us and said, look how wise and understanding these people are. We became very famous and had a strong reputation of being a wise people.

So whenever we got conquered and enslaved, the slave masters knew: even though we have them as captives, they ain't stupid, they're very smart, so we have to use them as best we can while we have them. It happened in Egypt, in Babylon, in Persia, with the Greeks and Romans, and with the white man in America and Africa, using the genius of the slaves and the colonized. That is why Babylon took Daniel and his fellows, the king's seed, to stand in the palace.

precepts.text: When your coworkers wondering why this brother don't murmur with them and don't ever work the Sabbath: keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people. The other nations are expecting you to be that greedy individual that lacks integrity, but we give them this right here.
precepts.point: This is how they infiltrate organizations, through money. Organizations fail because of money: they infiltrate, they come in, offer money, and they give up their organization. That mean they lacked integrity; they let money come in and dictate and control the movement. That ain't happening here.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
Judas is the character we are not to have. “This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag.” He walked with Christ and saw many miracles, and still betrayed the savior and everybody around him. Money was his root and his god: greed. That is how they infiltrate organizations: they come in and offer money, and a people lacking integrity gives up the organization and lets money dictate and control the movement. That ain't happening here.

Israel is to give the nations the opposite: “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” Keeping the law is our wisdom, and it is seen.

When your coworkers wonder why this brother doesn't murmur with them and never works the Sabbath, that is the nations seeing the statutes kept. The other nations are expecting you to be that greedy individual that lacks integrity, a Judas who can be bought. We give them this right here: character and integrity, the hidden strength behind wisdom.

precepts.text: And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations. Not in America, not in Florida: among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen. You know what that scripture is saying? No matter where you go, you're going to see Israelites. Pictures shown in class: Captain Joham just came from Trinidad and Suriname for Passover with the brothers.
precepts.point: They departed unto Seleucia, and from thence they sailed to Cyprus. He's showing you Paul traveled. What are we doing? We continue the Acts of the Apostles. And brothers, listen, we get a lot of hate for it. A lot of people hate us, but we don't care. We are doing the Most High God's work. We just came from all over the world keeping Passover, bringing the good news.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.why:
“Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.” When the Bishop says separate that brother for the work, he is not talking about Atlanta. He is not talking about Miami or California. Did Israel only scatter in Atlanta? Did Israel only scatter in America? Separate them for the work means no matter where the work is, you have to go there.

The prophecy shows where the work is: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations”. Not in America, not in Florida: among the nations. “and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” You know what that scripture is saying? No matter where you go, you are going to see Israelites. That is why a judge must be able to travel. Captain Joham just came from Trinidad and Suriname keeping Passover with the brothers there.

So the work Barnabas and Saul were separated for is the same work now: going to the nations where the Lord scattered Israel. It was the Most High God who called you, not the bishop, deacon or captain, and once hands are laid on you, you are sent away. When the phone call comes to travel, we do not want to hear anything from you but yes. Paul travelled, departing unto Seleucia and sailing to Cyprus, and we continue the Acts of the Apostles, bringing the good news all over the world, whatever hate we get for it.

precepts.text: Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. You never heard the Father's voice at any time in history. So that voice our people heard in the wilderness, and that shape the elders saw: that was Christ.
precepts.point: Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice: whose voice did they hear from the heavens? That was Christ's voice, speaking the commandments. And upon earth he shewed thee his great fire: when the Lord came down in Exodus, only the seventy elders saw his majesty; everybody else saw fire.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee”. Whose voice did they hear from the heavens? Some people think that is the Father. No, that was Christ's voice. That was the Lord speaking, the one who came down and gave us the commandments.

Christ said it himself: “And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.” The Father sent Christ and bore witness of him, but at no time in history have you ever heard the Father's voice, and you never saw his shape.

So the voice our people heard in the wilderness, out of the midst of the fire, was Christ's. And the shape the seventy elders saw when the Lord came down was Christ. It was always the Lord, always Christ there: the rock and the chariot that followed us, the one who came down and smote the Egyptians, the same one who will come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt that we are living in today.

precepts.text: See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. The one that spake on earth was Moses; the people said, we do not want God to speak to us, Moses, you tell us the commandments, because his voice shook the earth and they were terrified. Much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven: that was the Lord. Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven: that is when he returns in the future to shake the nations. For our God is a consuming fire: that is what the people saw when he came down on the mountain.
precepts.point: Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice: whose voice did they hear from the heavens? That was Christ's voice, speaking the commandments. And upon earth he shewed thee his great fire: when the Lord came down in Exodus, only the seventy elders saw his majesty; everybody else saw fire.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Paul speaks of the same thing Moses did in Deuteronomy 4. “See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth”: the one that spoke on earth is Moses. The people said, we do not want to hear God, lest we die; Moses, you tell us what he says. Moses gave us the laws, we refused them from Moses, and everybody was killed in the wilderness.

“much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven”. The one speaking from heaven was the Lord. “Whose voice then shook the earth”. When he spoke the commandments the earth was shaking, and that is why the people were terrified and said, Moses, you speak to us. “but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.” He is going to shake nations: that is when he returns in the future. The Lord already knew we would go off and that he would have to come again to deliver us. Then those things “which cannot be shaken may remain”, and we receive “a kingdom which cannot be moved”.

“For our God is a consuming fire.” Why does Paul say this? Because that is what the people saw. The Lord said, do not let anybody come near the mountain when I come down, because anyone who comes near will die. When he came down it was a consuming fire; that is all everybody saw, except the seventy elders, who had the Holy Spirit on them and saw his majesty. That is Deuteronomy 4:36: “upon earth he shewed thee his great fire; and thou heardest his words out of the midst of the fire”, the fire that issues forth from his throne.

precepts.text: Ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land; and the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen. Moses saw the Israelites scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves, and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will befall you in the latter days. Moses saw the latter days. Why can Moses say I know? Because God showed Moses what would happen to us: in the time of the Babylonians, the Greeks, the Romans, and here in America.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
In Deuteronomy 31 Moses says, “For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves”, and “evil will befall you in the latter days”. How is Moses able to say I know? Deuteronomy 4 shows what he saw.

“I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.” When we went into the land of Israel, our days were not going to be prolonged in it; we were going to be destroyed from off that land. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” Moses saw the Israelites being scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

He could see it because God showed it to him. In 2 Esdras 14, read right after, the Lord says, “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt”, and he held him on the mount a long season, the forty days and forty nights, and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Moses saw the secrets of the beginning, which is how he wrote Genesis, and he saw the end.

So Moses saw what would happen to us in the time of the Babylonians, the Greeks and the Romans, and he saw us here in America, in the transatlantic slave trade, and America being destroyed. That is why he could say with certainty that evil would befall us in the latter days: he had already seen it.

precepts.text: A great multitude which no man could number, of all nations, kindreds, people, and tongues. Christians use this to confuse you. Acts 2:5 shows Jews, devout men out of every nation under heaven, and Tobit 13:3-4 says confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel, for he hath scattered us among them. The multitude is Israelites out of every nation, and James wrote to the twelve tribes scattered abroad.
precepts.point: When thou art in tribulation and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord and be obedient, he is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee nor destroy thee, the lake of fire, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers. That is the crown of life of Revelation 2:10.
precepts.why:
“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb”. Christians go to Revelation 7:9 to try to confuse you. They say all people coming out of all nations means all peoples, every race, standing before the throne.

But Moses already told us who would be found in all nations: “the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”. That scattering was slavery, and we were left few in number because they were killing us. So a great multitude coming out of every nation and kindred and tongue is the scattered children of Israel, gathered back out of the lands they were taken to.

The precepts read right behind it settle it: Acts 2:5 shows Jews, devout men, “out of every nation under heaven”; Tobit 13 says “ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them”; Ezekiel 28:25 speaks of the Lord gathering “the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered”; and James wrote “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. The multitude before the throne is Israel out of every nation. If they confound you with Revelation 7:9 on the street, shame on you.

precepts.text: There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.
precepts.point: When thou art in tribulation and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord and be obedient, he is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee nor destroy thee, the lake of fire, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers. That is the crown of life of Revelation 2:10.
precepts.why:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” This answers the question of who the people of all nations, kindreds and tongues are. They were Jews, Israelites, and they came out of every nation under heaven.

That is exactly what Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 4: the Lord would scatter Israel among the nations. So when scripture shows a people coming out of every nation, it is not speaking of the nations themselves. It is speaking of Israel, found in every nation because the Lord scattered them there.

So Acts 2:5 is the key for Revelation 7:9. Out of every nation does not mean every nation's people; it means the devout Israelites dwelling among every nation, the same scattered people Deuteronomy 4:27 speaks of, who are seeking the Lord from thence.

precepts.text: Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel, for he hath scattered us among them; there declare his greatness and extol him before all the living. The same thing Moses said in Deuteronomy 4.
precepts.point: When thou art in tribulation and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord and be obedient, he is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee nor destroy thee, the lake of fire, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers. That is the crown of life of Revelation 2:10.
precepts.why:
“Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them.” Tobit is speaking to the children of Israel, and he tells us plainly where they are: scattered among the Gentiles. The Lord did the scattering, just as Moses said in Deuteronomy 4:27.

“There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Lord, and he is the God our Father for ever.” There, in those lands where we were scattered, declare his greatness. It is the same thing Moses said in Deuteronomy 4: “But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him”. From thence, from the lands we were taken to, we seek him, and we are seeking him now here in America and finding him.

So Tobit proves both halves of the opened scripture: Israel scattered among the Gentiles, and Israel turning to confess the Lord right there among them. He is our Lord, the God of our fathers for ever, and he has not forgotten the covenant of our fathers.

precepts.text: James, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. If Revelation 7:9 confounds you on the street, shame on you.
precepts.point: When thou art in tribulation and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord and be obedient, he is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee nor destroy thee, the lake of fire, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers. That is the crown of life of Revelation 2:10.
precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” James wrote his letter to the twelve tribes, and he says where they are: scattered abroad. The scattering Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 4:27 had already come upon them, and the apostles were writing to Israel in the nations.

It stands with Ezekiel 28:25, read in the same moment: “When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered, and shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the heathen, then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant Jacob.” Israel is scattered among the people, and the Lord gathers Israel out of them back to the land he gave Jacob.

So the great multitude out of all nations in Revelation 7:9 is the twelve tribes scattered abroad, gathered back. This is what you say when they try to tell you on the street that people coming out of all nations means all peoples. If you let them confound you with Revelation 7:9, shame on you.

precepts.text: Let him that stole steal no more, but labour that he may give to him that needeth.
precepts.point: Biblical economics aims at communal wealth so that no generation is left stuck, and Israel should deal that way with each other now.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.” If you get blessed, it is to have to give to him that needeth. That is biblical, and that is part of the wisdom of Deuteronomy 4:6: the laws, statutes and commandments, everything written in the scripture, are our wisdom and our understanding, and we are to govern and deal with each other based on what God says.

How is that giving set up? You read it in Acts 2 and Acts 4: you put it at the feet of the leadership, and the leadership distributes as there is need. The leaders in the body initiate everything by the scripture, with the fundraising initiatives and the different offices, so that the body can be self-sustaining.

But many of us were raised in this environment and have not sharpened our senses, so we conduct business like Esau. Israelite businesses pop up, market to the body and make money off the body, and never come back and say, my pockets have gotten filled, my business has become profitable, I want to give back. Some even have cutthroat tactics, with no type of respect, moving the same way the world moves.

Those who say they are businessmen should read how the economics in Israel functioned and how we dealt with each other. Debt was forgiven every seven years so that debt would not pass from generation to generation. There was no usury, meaning no interest. Today what people wind up leaving behind is debt, and their families become responsible for it.

So the righteous way is to labour, prosper, and give back to the needy among our people. That is the foundation for seeing how Babylon, Esau and the rest of the world move in buying and selling, and why a nation that keeps God's statutes would be called “a wise and understanding people.”

precepts.text: He is a merchant; the balances of deceit are in his hand.
precepts.point: Biblical economics aims at communal wealth so that no generation is left stuck, and Israel should deal that way with each other now.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“He is a merchant, the balances of deceit are in his hand: he loveth to oppress.” That spirit was in Israel as well, and this is spoken to us. Hosea deals primarily with the northern kingdom, with Judah mentioned in the mix.

Where did we learn it? Not from our own law. When you read the law and how we handled economics amongst ourselves, there was no such thing. We were mixed among the other nations and took on their customs: not only their lewdness and fornications, but how they would have no compassion on their people and how they dealt with them.

Usury was something we were supposed to do to the other nations: we lent to them and charged them interest. When we dealt with each other it was different. Not that you did not make a profit, but there were ways we dealt with each other, always with the intent that we would have communal wealth, so that generations would not get stuck with bad habits. We looked out for each other, the same way the corners of the field were left to help one another, and we were still able to prosper under that.

Instead we took up the insatiable appetite of the nations, having to get every last drop. Not so with God. That is why these balances of deceit were spoken against us. Keeping the statutes, dealing righteously with our brethren, is the wisdom Deuteronomy 4:6 says the nations will one day see in us.

precepts.text: Making the ephah small and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit.
precepts.point: Biblical economics aims at communal wealth so that no generation is left stuck, and Israel should deal that way with each other now.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?” That is messing with the scales. It is the same spirit of deceitful balances read in Hosea 12:7, and it was spoken against us because we had mixed among the other nations and learned it from them.

Remember when Nehemiah had to curse out the merchants from the other nations because they came to sell on the sabbath. If we had all been in the spirit, would he have had to curse them out? We would not have bought, and they would not have come. They came because we were breaking the law by buying.

We should not have that spirit, but now you see who really does. One of the grand ways they falsify the balances today is with the oil: they call Venezuela's crude too heavy, while it is more profitable to them than anything else.

It reaches into the mortgage too. Interest is designed to keep you in debt and keep you broke, and the mortgage is loaded front heavy, so the first years go mostly to interest and not principal. On a 300,000 home a 30-year loan costs an extra 250,800, and instead of fixing the economy Trump talks about a 50-year mortgage, where you pay an additional 476,000 just to have a cheaper payment, and leave that debt to your wife and kids. That is the deceit. When we think of scales we think of the little scale at the fruit market, but this shows how broad that evil principle is. Edom does it first, and they excel at it.

It is not wrong to own a home; it is better than renting. But the system is broken and was never supposed to be that way. If our economics were set up by the law, we would lend to each other without usury and own our homes. Even to that extent the Lord had righteous weights, scales and balances, and that is the wisdom and understanding Deuteronomy 4:6 speaks of.

precepts.text: The covenant that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law: so covenant, law and wisdom are all the same thing.
precepts.point: So wisdom and the commandments are interchangeable, and it is the statutes the nations hear that make us a wise and understanding people.

precepts.text: What thing soever I command you, observe to do it; observing to do it is obligated, not optional, and thou shalt not add thereto nor diminish from it.
precepts.point: The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove Matthew 18:11 and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.
precepts.why:
Moses says it again: “What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.” Observing to do it is obligated, not optional, and the charge is the same as here: “Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it”.

This was spoken around 1500 BC, and on the last page of the Bible the same charge closes the book. The prophets across millenniums and captivities all speak the same thing, Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ and John, and that consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes.

precepts.text: If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues written in this book, and if any man take away from the words, God shall take away his part out of the book of life.
precepts.point: The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove Matthew 18:11 and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.
precepts.why:
On the last page of the Bible the charge Moses gave around 1500 BC closes the book: “If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city”.

Moses said neither add unto the word nor diminish ought from it; John says the same thing across millenniums and captivities. That consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes.

Taking away is what the watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show: many of them remove Matthew 18:11 and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha. Adding sounds like god loves everybody. Both carry a judgment: the plagues written in the book for the one who adds, and his part taken out of the book of life for the one who takes away.

precepts.text: That ye all speak the same thing: John the Revelator and Moses were speaking the same thing, and Christ spoke out of the Old Testament.
precepts.point: The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove Matthew 18:11 and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.
precepts.why:
“Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.”

That is what the prophets did. John the Revelator and Moses were speaking the same thing, neither add nor diminish, and Christ spoke out of the Old Testament. Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ and John, across millenniums and captivities, all speak the same thing, perfectly joined together in the same mind and the same judgment. That consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes.

So we speak the same thing too: not adding to the word and not diminishing from it, that there be no divisions among us.

precepts.text: Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.
precepts.why:
“Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.” Adding to the word sounds like god loves everybody: how many have been found liars saying it?

Do not quote what the Most High has not said. An opinion off the top of your head cannot be proven by scripture, and the one who adds it to his words is reproved and found a liar. That is the weight behind “Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you”.

precepts.text: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool; following your own mind instead of the scripture is folly.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.
precepts.why:
“He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.” Following your own mind instead of the scripture is folly.

An opinion off the top of your head cannot be proven by scripture, and the man who trusts that heart and adds it to the word is a fool. Whoso walks wisely, by the word as it was commanded, neither adding nor diminishing, shall be delivered.

precepts.text: Prove all things; if you cannot prove it, do not utter it.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.
precepts.why:
“Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.” If you cannot prove it, do not utter it.

An opinion off the top of your head cannot be proven by scripture, and adding it to the word is what Moses forbids. Do not quote what the Most High has not said; prove it from the scripture, and hold fast that which is good.

precepts.text: If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God, neither adding nor taking away.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.
precepts.why:
“If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God”. To speak as the oracles of God is to speak neither adding nor taking away, only what the Most High has said.

New brothers in this truth should not rush to debate before they have studied to shew themselves approved; uttering things that are not in the scriptures is not a good look. Speak as the oracles of God, “that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ”.

precepts.text: Speak all the words that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a word.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.
precepts.why:
From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word. Jeremiah was told: “Stand in the court of the Lord’s house, and speak unto all the cities of Judah, which come to worship in the Lord’s house, all the words that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a word”.

All the words, not some of them. So do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity. Moses, Jeremiah, Christ and John all carry the same charge: neither add nor diminish.

precepts.text: These caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass in the matter of Peor; that history stands behind this verse.
precepts.point: The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.
precepts.why:
“Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal–peor”. That recalls the history of Balaam. Balaam was a Midianite, an Ishmaelite, and it was through his counsel that Israel fell: “Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.”

That history stands behind this verse. The plague is how “all the men that followed Baal–peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them from among you.” But those who said they would not go after that foolishness were saved alive: “ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day.”

The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes and commandments and have life.

precepts.text: I call heaven and earth to record: life and death, blessing and cursing, are set before you, so choose life; everything is being recorded, every idle word.
precepts.point: The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.
precepts.why:
“I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live”. Everything is being recorded, every idle word.

Baal-peor showed both sides of it: “all the men that followed Baal–peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them”, and “ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day.” Death for those who followed that foolishness, life for those who cleaved to him.

The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions. Keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes and commandments and have life. Life and death are set before you, so choose life.

precepts.text: Evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repayed; the Most High does not bless a man in his sins, and the trouble that keeps following is the pursuit of sin.
precepts.point: The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.
precepts.why:
“Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.” The Most High does not bless a man in his sins, and the trouble that keeps following is the pursuit of sin.

The men that followed Baal-peor were pursued by that evil until the Lord destroyed them from among the people, while those that cleaved unto the Lord were repaid with life, alive every one of them that day. It is that simple: follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes and commandments and have life.

precepts.text: A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people: Peter and Moses speak the same thing about the same people.
precepts.point: Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.
precepts.why:
“But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”. Peter and Moses speak the same thing about the same people.

Peculiar by definition means characteristic of only one person, group or thing, and different from the usual or normal. When Israel keeps the laws it makes them a peculiar nation: the Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations. That is “your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations”.

Royal means of a kingly ancestry, and the King of kings is Christ. But rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. When Israel is fallen into sin, the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding. Keep the statutes and judgments, and the nations see a royal priesthood, an holy nation, and say “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”

precepts.text: Of Adam come we all, and there is also the people whom the Most High hath chosen, the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.
precepts.why:
“And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” Of Adam come we all, and then there is also the people whom the Most High hath chosen, the children of Israel.

That is the people Moses is speaking to: a people chosen out of all that came of Adam, and set apart by the statutes and judgments. Keeping them “is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations”. Israel deals with the Almighty; having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at.

precepts.text: Thou art an holy people, chosen to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations upon the earth; Deuteronomy 7 likewise calls Israel special and above all nations.
precepts.point: Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.
precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” Deuteronomy 7 likewise calls Israel special and above all nations.

Peculiar means characteristic of only one person, group or thing, and different from the usual or normal. The Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations, and keeping the laws is what makes them so. That is why “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations”. Israel deals with the Almighty, and having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at.

precepts.text: When the laws are broken Israel is made a reproach to the neighbours, a scorn and a derision, a byword among the heathen, and a shaking of the head among the people; calling ourselves colors and bywords instead of our nationality is part of that estate.
precepts.point: Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.
precepts.why:
The other side of the same coin. When the laws are broken: “Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us. Thou makest us a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head among the people.”

When Israel keeps the statutes the nations say “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” When Israel is fallen into sin the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding: a reproach, a scorn and a derision, a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head. Calling ourselves colors and bywords instead of our nationality is part of that estate.

Rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. They may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

precepts.text: And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee? The first thing named is to fear the Lord thy God; that fear proves the love, the confession, and the spirit.
precepts.point: Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.
precepts.why:
“And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee, but to fear the Lord thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the Lord thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul”. The first thing named is to fear the Lord thy God.

Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: that fear proves the love, the confession and the spirit. Fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

That is why the Most High gathered the people at Horeb, “that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children.” Why learn to fear him? Verses 3 and 4 of this same chapter answer it: those that followed the idols were destroyed, and those that cleaved to him are alive. Follow after idols, after the nations and their religions, and he will destroy you.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.
precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

It begins with fear. That is why at Horeb the Most High gathered the people “that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth”. Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession; fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says. The good understanding belongs to them that do his commandments.

And these are generational commandments: “teach them thy sons, and thy sons’ sons”, children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat, and the fear that is the beginning of wisdom is taught to the children.

precepts.text: Two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God; Deuteronomy 4:13 is the reiteration of this, for Deuteronomy means repetition.
precepts.point: And he wrote them upon two tables of stone. The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses; they were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever.
precepts.why:
“And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God.” Deuteronomy 4:13 is the reiteration of this, for Deuteronomy means repetition: “he declared unto you his covenant, which he commanded you to perform, even ten commandments; and he wrote them upon two tables of stone.”

The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses. They were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever. The ten are the umbrella over all the other commandments, the sub-laws and sub-statutes beneath them.

precepts.text: With Moses the Most High spake mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; that is why Israel saw no similitude and heard plain commandments.
precepts.point: Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.
precepts.why:
“If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream. My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house. With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches”.

That is why Israel “saw no manner of similitude on the day that the Lord spake unto you in Horeb”. No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches. When the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant: fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill. It was simple and easy to understand.

So Israel is charged to take good heed, “Lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female”. Plain commandments leave no room for the graven images of Egypt.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war: a man. The scriptures give no ground to those who say God is a woman; he deals with the men of Israel, and no woman is to usurp authority over the man.
precepts.point: Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.
precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” A man. The scriptures give no ground to those who say God is a woman.

Israel had come out of Egypt, where graven images filled the land and where the likeness of the female was worshipped. Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there. So the Most High had to say plainly, no “likeness of male or female”, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

The Lord is a man of war. He deals with the men of Israel, and no woman is to usurp authority over the man.

precepts.text: The Most High giveth the sun for a light by day and the ordinances of the moon and stars for a light by night; if those ordinances depart from before him, then the seed of Israel shall cease from being a nation. They serve his children, not the reverse.
precepts.point: Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.
precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night”. The sun, moon and stars are ordinances: they keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept.

“If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.” They serve his children, not the reverse. So why worship what the Most High created to serve you? Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept, not the sun, moon and stars.

That is the warning here: “lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them”. That is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac and witchcraft today. Calling yourself a Gemini or a Taurus is the same star worship; none of it is the way to the kingdom, and it was filth learned in Egypt.

precepts.text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools: put off the filth learned in this land and drop the prideful rebuttals of the lies you were taught.
precepts.point: Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.
precepts.why:
“Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.”

The likeness of beast, fowl, creeping thing and fish were the gods learned in Egypt: Heqet the frog god, Sobek the god of the river, Horus the falcon, the beetles, flies and locusts they deified, and Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians. The sun, moon and stars were Ra and Nut, and today astrology and the zodiac. It was filth learned in Egypt, and this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her.

So coming to the house of God, put off the filth learned in this land and drop the prideful rebuttals of the lies you were taught. Be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools, who consider not that they do evil.

precepts.text: Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground; Moses knew all the ways and deities of the Egyptians, and he was told to be quiet, humble himself, and receive the milk of the laws so he could grow.
precepts.point: Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.
precepts.why:
“Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.”

Moses knew all the ways and deities of the Egyptians, the beasts, fowls, creeping things and fish they deified, and the sun, the moon and the stars they worshipped. And he was told to be quiet, humble himself, and receive the milk of the laws so he could grow.

That is the posture for coming out of the idols of Egypt: what was learned in that land is filth, and it is put off at the door like the shoes from off the feet, for the place is holy ground.

precepts.text: The Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods, wood and stone; the same prophecy in the curses.
precepts.point: And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.
precepts.why:
The same prophecy stands in the curses: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

Deuteronomy 4:27 is future prophecy of the scattering to the four corners of the earth, “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”. And in those lands “ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone”. The wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca, gods which neither Israel nor their fathers had known. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

precepts.text: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia: the scattered ones are Israel.
precepts.point: And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.
precepts.why:
“Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”. The scattered ones are Israel.

Moses prophesied it: “the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”. Peter writes to those very strangers, scattered among the nations. And it is in the lands of the scattering that Israel would serve gods of wood and stone, the cross of christianity and the kaaba stone at Mecca.

precepts.text: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake unto the fathers by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son; Christ's coming began the last days, and the Most High has always dealt through his prophets.
precepts.point: For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.
precepts.why:
“God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son”. The Most High has always dealt through his prophets, and Christ's coming began the last days.

That tells you when “the latter days” are: they began when Christ came. “When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice”. This is that time, and the turning begins with the spirit of fear, to get right with the Most High, seeking him with all thy heart and with all thy soul.

precepts.text: Thou shalt therefore obey the voice of the Lord thy God, and do his commandments and his statutes; that is what the voice of God tells a man to do.
precepts.point: For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt therefore obey the voice of the Lord thy God, and do his commandments and his statutes, which I command thee this day.” That is what the voice of God tells a man to do: keep his commandments.

So when it says “if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice”, that voice tells you to keep his commandments. If someone claims God spoke to him in a dream and told him everything but obedience, that is not the voice of the Most High.

precepts.text: Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of the word; doing his commandments is hearkening to that voice.
precepts.point: For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.
precepts.why:
“Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” Doing his commandments is hearkening to that voice.

Even the angels show it: to hearken unto the voice of the word is to do his commandments. So to be “obedient unto his voice” in the latter days is to keep his commandments; and “the Lord thy God is a merciful God”, he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

precepts.text: Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers; looking up the history is a command, not a fixation.
precepts.point: Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.
precepts.why:
“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Looking up the history is a command, not a fixation.

Moses says the same: “ask now of the days that are past, which were before thee, since the day that God created man upon the earth”. You are supposed to search out your forefathers and look up your history, and not slavery only: the reign under David and Solomon and the empires where Israel ruled, and slavery too, because failing to keep the laws is why the people went into it.

Search it and there is no such history anywhere else. No other people heard the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire and lived; no other nation was taken from the midst of another nation “by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand”. The Most High did this for Israel alone, “that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.”

precepts.text: Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen; the chosen seed the whole passage speaks of.
precepts.point: Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it, for Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.
precepts.why:
“Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen”. This is the chosen seed the whole passage speaks of: “because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out in his sight with his mighty power out of Egypt”.

He drove out nations greater and mightier than Israel, with more economic might and more military power, but the Most High delivered Israel out of their hands, and to this day the twelve tribes are still here.

“Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart”. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it. Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, Jacob his servant, Israel whom he has chosen, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: Israel was warned not to corrupt themselves by worshipping the host of heaven.

The Most High commanded Moses at that time to teach the statutes and judgments, and Israel is charged to take good heed, for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day the Lord spake in Horeb.

The likeness of any beast on the earth goes back to idols like Heqet the frog god and Sobek the god of the river; the likeness of any winged fowl to Horus the falcon; anything that creepeth on the ground to the beetles, flies, and locusts they deified; any fish in the waters to Sobek and to Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians, whose symbolism carries into pagan imagery to this day.

Lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven and be driven to worship the sun, the moon, and the stars: that is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac, and witchcraft today. The Lord hath taken you and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance.

Moses must die in this land and not go over Jordan, but ye shall go over and possess that good land; he kept repeating it, longing for what he would not see.
